title: DepEd gives Antipolo teachers laptops, tech training

blocks.text: The Department of Education (DepEd) has launched a hands-on technology training program for public school teachers alongside its nationwide distribution of laptops, as part of efforts to accelerate digitalization in basic education.

Education Secretary Sonny Angara led the launch of GuroXL, a customized professional development program, during the distribution of laptops to 1,441 public school teachers from 62 schools in Antipolo City.
The teachers received MacBook Neo laptops under the DepEd Computerization Program (DCP) and immediately participated in guided training sessions on how to use the devices for classroom instruction.

"What this is all about is giving you the best that we can give you. Because we know teachers give their best, even without laptops, you give everything you can and go above and beyond what is required. That is why you continue to inspire us, and the President is behind you one hundred percent. We at DepEd are behind you one hundred percent," Angara said.

“Please maximize these tools because there is so much that they can do for you and for your learners. Let us take time to listen because they will explain to you the potential, and they will make you more productive, save you time, and enable you to be a better teacher,” he added.
The rollout builds on the nationwide laptop distribution program launched by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Angara in Dagupan City on November 9.

DepEd has awarded contracts for 231,725 teacher laptops, consisting of 169,008 MacBook Neo units and 62,717 Windows-based laptops. Another 3,646 MacBook Neo units were procured for administrative officers.
The delivery and deployment of the devices are expected to continue through March 2027.

Coordinated through the National Educators Academy of the Philippines (NEAP), the DepEd Information and Communications Technology Service, and the Bureau of Learning Delivery, GuroXL allows teachers to train using the same laptops assigned to them.
The laptop packages were procured through competitive public bidding at approximately P43,000 per unit, significantly below suggested retail prices.
Each package includes a five-year warranty, built-in productivity software, logistics, technical support and professional development assistance.
DepEd said the nationwide rollout aims to narrow the digital divide in public education while reducing teachers' administrative workload.—LDF, GMA News
